Use BOTH general-lambda estimates of 038: give E||Z_1(h)||_lambda^2 <= R_alpha h^2 lambda^{alpha-2}(1+lambda^2 h^2)^2 N^2, and through S_0(-h) the first random term is charged e times this first coefficient, giving e R_alpha h^2 lambda^{alpha-2}(1+lambda^2 h^2)^2 N^2; the mean second-order term is charged 2N sqrt e times ||E Z_2(h)||_lambda, giving 2 sqrt e D_Gamma (1+lambda^2 h^2) h^{3-alpha} N^2/[lambda(2-alpha)(3-alpha)]; this yields L_alpha(h,lambda)=4e R_alpha h^2 lambda^{alpha-2} + [4 sqrt e D_Gamma/((2-alpha)(3-alpha))] h^{3-alpha}/lambda at lambda h<=1, with no favorable mean sign.
For n>=1, norm comparisons and the 042 factorial bound give ||Y_n||_{L2(Omega;X_lambda)} <= [sqrt e/(lambda h)] (A_alpha sqrt(R_alpha))^n h^{(4-alpha)n/2}/(n!)^{gamma/2} N.

Orthogonal Gaussian parity (colors/parity on the same field) gives E<Y_r,Y_s>_lambda=0 for r+s odd; for r+s=2k use r!s!>=(k!)^2 and the split count 2k+1 to bound the sum of absolute inner products by [e(2k+1)/(lambda h)^2] (A_alpha^2 R_alpha)^k h^{(4-alpha)k}/(k!)^gamma N^2, with the all-factors construction from 042; the k>=2 tail is dominated by (lambda h)^{-2} x^2 e^{gamma x^{1/gamma}} with x=B_alpha sigma^2 R_alpha h^{4-alpha}, B_alpha=3 e A_alpha^2, after keeping the sharper first coefficient.

Combining the first-coefficient term and the higher-even-order tail gives E||I^eps_sigma(h)(f,g)||_lambda^2 <= [1+sigma^2 L_alpha(h,lambda)+(lambda h)^{-2} x^2 e^{gamma x^{1/gamma}}]||(f,g)||_lambda^2, the displayed C:static-interaction bound.

For the dyadic clause sigma_j^2=h_j^{-alpha_0}, h_j=2^{-j}/lambda, verify the first coefficient terms after T/h_j are constant multiples of T lambda^{alpha-2} h_j^{1-alpha_0} and (T/lambda) h_j^{2-alpha-alpha_0}, both manifestly positive powers for alpha_0<1 and alpha+alpha_0<2; the higher-order term is (T/lambda^2)(B_alpha R_alpha)^2 h_j^{2 beta-3} times a bounded exponential factor at h_0, with beta=4-alpha-alpha_0>2 so 2 beta-3>0; the geometric dyadic series converges.

For the finite-partition tensor bound, per step M_j(h_j)=S_0(h_j)I_j(h_j) with independent successive fields; the static map has a bounded L2 extension to deterministic initial phases and is tensored by the past probability space to allow random initial phases INDEPENDENT of the j-th field; iterating gives the product of e^{lambda h_j}[1+E(h_j,sigma_j,lambda)] and hence E||M_K...M_1(f,g)||_lambda^2 <= exp{lambda sum_j h_j + sum_j E(...)}||(f,g)||_lambda^2; each block develops its own field only over its one block and is independent of the NEXT field, while the dyadic scalar summability is one upper-bound sum, not a product representation for overlapping/repeated fields.
